title: How Long Should a Man's Legs Be? Grounded Wisdom
summary: 'How long should a man's legs be?' asked the reporter. 'Long enough to reach from his body to the ground!' replied Lincoln.
keywords: How Long Should a Man's Legs Be? Grounded Wisdom
full_text:
At six feet four inches tall, Abraham Lincoln towered over his contemporaries. His disproportionately long legs and angular gait were frequent targets of political caricaturists, who depicted him as an awkward giraffe.

During an 1860 press conference, a journalist decided to have some fun at Lincoln's expense.

Stepping forward with mock seriousness, the reporter asked:
"Mr. Lincoln! There has been a spirited debate among anatomists regarding proper human proportions. In your esteemed opinion, how long ought a man's legs to be?"

The room fell quiet, expecting Lincoln to take offense or offer an elaborate physiological defense.

Lincoln looked down at his long limbs, adjusted his necktie, and answered with dry frontier simplicity:

**"Well, friend, I have given that matter some considerable study.
And I have come to the conclusion that a man's legs ought to be long enough to reach from his body to the ground!"**

The room exploded with laughter!

In one masterstroke, Lincoln exposed the absurdity of superficial vanity. What matters is not whether one's limbs are aesthetically pleasing according to fashion plates, but whether they serve their natural purpose: keeping a man firmly grounded on this earth.
moral: Never let others shake your confidence through superficial mockery; practical common sense is the ultimate antidote to vanity.
